Korn Ferry delivered a strong finish to fiscal year 2026, with full-year fee revenue reaching $2.91 billion to $2.94 billion (depending on reporting classification), representing a 7% year-over-year increase [4], [7]. Net income expanded 14% to approximately $277.4 million, pushing the net margin to 9.4–9.6%, up from 8.9% in FY25, primarily driven by operating leverage and higher revenue rather than cost-cutting alone [2], [4], [7].

Adjusted EBITDA margin in Q4 reached 16.9%, exceeding analyst estimates by 0.9 percentage points [10].

Management has adopted a measured near-term stance. For Q1 FY27, the company guided fee revenue to $725 million–$745 million (midpoint ~$735 million), implying roughly 2.7% year-over-year growth [3], [10]. This midpoint fell slightly below some sell-side estimates (~$744.8 million) and was partially weighed down by softness in the Digital segment, though GAAP EPS guidance of $1.35 still beat consensus by 3.8% [8], [10]. 

Looking beyond FY26, analyst projections forecast revenue to grow at a 3.1%–4.0% annualized rate over the next three years, which notably lags behind the broader U.S. professional services industry growth forecast of 5.9%–6.7% [4], [10].
